cards.text: In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, a prophet, and he's the one telling it. It's one more message about Egypt, after a whole string of them in the chapters before (Ezekiel 29:1-32:16).
God calls him "Son of man" and gives him news about the multitudes of Egypt. Egypt is on its way out, and this is NOT good news.

cards.question: With news that heavy, what does God tell Ezekiel to do for the multitudes of Egypt?
Egypt won't go alone. The daughters of the mighty nations go with her. Where does God tell Ezekiel to consign them?

answers.text: To the depths of the earth

cards.text: Then comes a question for Egypt: "Whom do you surpass in beauty?" Friend, that's the kind of question where you don't answer. You just stare at your shoes.

cards.question: Right after asking whom Egypt surpasses in beauty, the message says, "Go down and be placed with the uncircumcised!" True or false: Egypt is being told she stands above the rest.

cards.text: Those going down will fall among those slain by the sword. Then the message rings out: "The sword is appointed!"

cards.question: The message says, "Let them drag her away…" True or false: Egypt's multitudes go along with her.

cards.text: From the middle of Sheol, someone speaks up about Egypt and her allies: "They have come down and lie with the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword."

cards.question: Down in Sheol, who speaks up about Egypt and her allies coming down?

cards.text: Then the message shows who's already down there. First is Assyria, a mighty empire, with her whole company and her graves all around her in the depths of the Pit.

cards.question: Assyria's whole company lies around her graves in the Pit. How did every one of them get there?

cards.text: Assyria's company are "those who once spread terror in the land of the living." Next is Elam, a nation far to the east, with all her multitudes around her grave.

cards.question: Elam's multitudes once spread their terror in the land of the living too. True or false: down in the Pit, they bear their disgrace.

cards.text: Among the slain, a resting place is prepared for Elam and all her hordes. Then come Meshech and Tubal, two peoples who traded with Tyre (Ezekiel 27:13), with all their multitudes and their graves all around them.
Then there are the fallen warriors of old. They went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, their swords placed under their heads and their shields resting on their bones.

cards.question: True or false: Meshech and Tubal lie down with the fallen warriors of old, the ones who went down to Sheol with their swords placed under their heads.
Partway through the list of nations, the message turns and speaks to "you." What will happen to "you"?

answers.text: You will be spared this time
You will rule over them all

cards.question: Edom, Israel's neighbor, is there too, with all her kings and princes. True or false: their might keeps them out from among those slain by the sword.

cards.text: All the leaders of the north and all the Sidonians, the people of the coastal city of Sidon, are there too, gone down in disgrace with the slain. Then Pharaoh, Egypt's king, slain by the sword with all his army, will see them all.

cards.question: When Pharaoh sees all these nations in the Pit, what does God say happens to him?

answers.text: He will cry out for help

cards.question: Then God has the last word, and the line about terror in the land of the living comes back one more time. Whose terror is it now?

cards.text: So Pharaoh and all his multitude will be laid to rest among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD. I think this one is heavy, friend.
